solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Meek sort, note, before start of hernia operation, gets meaty boner

parts.note: the lamb is the proverbial meek creature
C is a musical note

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of hernia
OP is the usual short form of operation

explanation.surface: A timid patient goes in for a hernia operation and comes out with something rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meaty boner' is Private Eye smut, but read innocently it is a cut of meat with a bone in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb chop is a cut of meat attached to a rib bone, so it is literally a meaty thing with a bone.

clue.text: One took out "one's offspring"?

parts.note: the indefinite article an means one
to draw out, as a sword or money, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone escorted the Queen's child on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is how the Queen famously referred to herself, so 'one's offspring' is one of her children.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew is a son of Queen Elizabeth II, the royal 'one' of the joke.

clue.text: "Gore twat" is hardly a circulation booster

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
a clot is a stupid person, a milder insult

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a politician named Gore is no help to a newspaper's sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulation booster' suggests newspaper sales; the definition means the blood's circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A thickened lump of blood obstructs flow in a vessel, the opposite of improving blood circulation.

clue.text: Full of amphetamines, she screwed novelist

indicators.note: something screwed up is twisted out of shape, so the letters are scrambled
being full of something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
Es are ecstasy pills, an amphetamine-type drug

explanation.surface: A drugged-up woman went to bed with a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse was the German-Swiss author of Steppenwolf and Siddhartha.

clue.text: Sexual manipulation taking advantage of pouch in pants

definitions.text: Sexual manipulation taking advantage of pouch in pants

parts.words: Sexual manipulation taking advantage of pouch in pants
parts.note: surface reading: a sordid act of groping through clothing
setter's reading: a trouser pocket, through which a man fiddles with himself, named after a cue game played on a table with pockets

explanation.surface: Someone is fondled with a hand slipped into a trouser pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang for a man playing with himself through his trouser pocket, and also the name of a cue game.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase pictures hands in trouser pockets fiddling with the balls, as in a cue game with pockets.

clue.text: A ponce's fancy hood

indicators.note: fancy as a verb is to imagine, so the letters are freely reimagined

parts.note: all six letters used

explanation.surface: A pimp has a liking for a hooded garment.
explanation.walkthrough: A ponce is British slang for a pimp. 'Hood' looks like headgear but is short for hoodlum.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the most famous Chicago gangster, and hood is slang for a gangster.

clue.text: Thatcher, bo, urged housing (town)

indicators.note: words housing something hold it inside them, so the letters sit within the phrase

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Mrs Thatcher was pressed, mate, to back council housing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bo is a matey form of address; the bracketed '(town)' is the definition, tucked where it barely reads as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherbourg is a port town on the Normandy coast of France.

clue.text: Ex-president prone to get blown

indicators.note: something blown apart is scattered, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: all five letters used

explanation.surface: A former leader lies down for a sex act.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan Perón was twice president of Argentina, so he is a former head of state.

clue.text: Vulgarly said excitement quite lacking, knickers, say, being unadorned?

indicators.note: said in a coarse accent that turns TH into F, so we follow the pronunciation

parts.note: with no excitement at all, as a Cockney would say it

explanation.surface: Plain underwear is dull, says someone crudely.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney and Estuary speech say F for TH, so thrills comes out as frills; frilly knickers are the joke picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no frills is plain and basic, lacking decorative extras.

clue.text: Party-backed records of borrowing getting up one's nose

indicators.note: backed means put in reverse, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a do is a party
IOUs are written notes of debt

explanation.surface: A political party funded by loans is annoying people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party-backed' sounds like political sponsorship; it is the word for a party turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting up one's nose is British idiom for irritating, and odious means repulsive and hateful.

clue.text: Getting close, organ having bad smell — leave

parts.note: CL is the street-address abbreviation for Close
the organ of hearing
food that has gone off smells bad

explanation.surface: As someone gets near, a smelly body part makes them want to go.
explanation.walkthrough: A close is a British dead-end street, abbreviated CL in addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear off is a rude command to go away, so it means leave as an imperative.

clue.text: Like cheap necklace on organ that might be kept on suspicious type

definitions.text: that might be kept on suspicious type

parts.note: a cheap necklace is made of beads
the organ of sight

explanation.surface: A trinket worn on a part of the body that a shady character might keep.
explanation.definitionFit: You keep a beady eye on someone you distrust, watching them closely and sharply.

clue.text: The beach is good in Martinique when having girl

parts.note: French for good, French being spoken in Martinique
a short girl's name, as in Princess Di

explanation.surface: A Caribbean beach is lovely when you have a woman with you.
explanation.walkthrough: Martinique is a French Caribbean island, so its word for good is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondi is Sydney's world-famous surf beach in Australia.

clue.text: John Bull's last pair of balls

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of Bull
two round letters shaped like balls

explanation.surface: The national figure John Bull's final pair of testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John Bull' looks like one name, but John is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: John is American slang for a toilet, and a loo is the British word for one.

clue.text: Boozing put out one's hip (second time)

indicators.note: a joint put out is dislocated, so the letters are knocked out of place

parts.note: all seven letters used
S is the abbreviation for second
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A drinker dislocates their hip for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: On the piss is coarse British slang for out drinking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the piss means going out for a heavy drinking session.

clue.text: Like porn? — ring producer, flower!

parts.note: blue means smutty, as in a blue movie
a bell is what rings

explanation.surface: Something smutty, a ring-maker and a bloom shouted in a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring producer' might suggest a jeweller; it is whatever makes a ringing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebell is a woodland plant with blue bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: "Testicle twitch" is internalised — and being worked up makes one "go" so

definitions.text: being worked up makes one "go" so

indicators.note: something internalised is taken inside, so this word goes into the middle of the others

parts.note: a ball is a testicle
a tic is an involuntary twitch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch in one's privates is kept quiet, and anger makes one move.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the idiom 'go ballistic': getting worked up makes one go this way.
explanation.definitionFit: To go ballistic is to fly into a rage, so getting angry sends one off that way.

clue.text: Court demand — get knackered again

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the umpire's call at Wimbledon, '..., please'
second meaning: knackers are testicles, so to be knackered again is to be given fresh ones

explanation.surface: A legal ruling says someone must be worn out once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law but is a tennis court; knackered normally means exhausted, here read as castrated, so new ones are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis fresh balls are called for at set intervals, and the second reading jokes about replacement testicles.

clue.text: Immersed in Attlee fiasco, Tony half abstaining

indicators.note: a fiasco is a total mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder
something immersed in another is sunk inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the six letters rearranged

indicators.note: half of a word means only its first two of four letters survive

parts.note: half of the four-letter name, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, caught up in an Attlee-style disaster, half gives up the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Attlee was Britain's postwar Labour prime minister, and Tony is Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person abstains completely from alcohol.

clue.text: Set to get leg over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is all ready to have sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get one's leg over' is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to set firm, as a jelly or plan does.

clue.text: Work hard, Fanny

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... away is to toil busily
second meaning: vulgar slang for the female genitals

explanation.surface: An order to someone called Fanny to put in more effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny looks like a name being addressed; in British slang it is the vulgar word for the vulva, not the bottom as in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The rodent is famously industrious, and the animal's name is also crude slang for female genitalia.

clue.text: Archer's thing: "I anticipate at last being a pioneering hero"

parts.note: an archer shoots with a bow
taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word, which alone is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of anticipate

explanation.surface: An archer's boast that they foresee being a trailblazing champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer may suggest Jeffrey Archer the novelist, a Private Eye target; it is just a bowman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Bowie was a frontiersman who died a hero at the Alamo, giving his name to the Bowie knife.

clue.text: Revolver wife put against arse

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
arse is British slang for a contemptible person, as is heel

explanation.surface: A gun is held to a spouse's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' looks like a pistol; it is anything that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns round on its axle, so it is literally a thing that revolves.

clue.text: Troublemaker wants broadcast undermined

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
a programme broadcast has been aired

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker wants a programme on TV to sabotage something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired is weakened or damaged, just as something undermined is.

clue.text: Played against King, Mother Nature's top spinner

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for played in sports tables
R is for Rex, Latin for king
an informal word for mother

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter, so just that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Nature

explanation.surface: A cricketer played against the King, and Mother Nature is the best spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top spinner' sounds like a cricket bowler; the definition is just 'spinner', someone who spins stories for the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A public relations man puts a favourable spin on news, so he is a spin doctor.

clue.text: (& 26ac.) Limit euro-voter's movement — hidden agenda?

indicators.note: movement means shifting about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: all fourteen letters used

explanation.surface: Curbing European voters' free movement betrays a secret plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' poses as free movement of people in the EU; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is a concealed reason behind an action, which is what a hidden agenda is.

clue.text: see 25ac.
Book handily obscures Salman's opening inside

indicators.note: to obscure something is to hide it, here by wrapping round it
inside confirms that one piece sits within the other

parts.note: palms are the insides of the hands, so they are what handily suggests

indicators.note: 'opening' keeps only the first letter of 'Salman'

parts.note: the first letter of Salman

explanation.surface: A book conveniently hides Salman Rushdie's opening chapter inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Salman suggests Rushdie and his notorious book; the wordplay needs only his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of sacred songs.

clue.text: Fast to grab fashionable, cushy job

indicators.note: to grab something is to clutch it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: fast as in held firm, securely fixed
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone quickly lands a trendy, easy position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed but means firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post requiring little or no work, the classic easy number.
